title: Starchforce — Potato Carbon Storage and Release Model
status: archive-generated biological stock-flow descendant of the Starchforce motif
maturity: T2 calculable biological toy model; not yet calibrated
abstract: This record turns the scientifically useful core of Starchforce into a conventional biological stock-flow model for potato tuber carbohydrate storage. The model treats a measurable storage pool K(t), an input flux J_in(t), a release or mobilization flux J_out(t), and non-target loss Gamma K. Its purpose is to create a model that can be calibrated, compared with simpler baselines and rejected if unnecessary. It does not propose a fifth fundamental force. Potato tubers are a natural flagship domain because starch is their major storage carbohydrate and a principal energy reserve. The project-specific contribution is the storage/release framing and its linkage to the Potato vocabulary; the balance equations themselves are ordinary stock-flow mathematics.
research_question: Can a small stock-flow model predict a declared potato tuber starch or carbohydrate time series better than simpler persistence or exponential baselines, and are its release and loss parameters identifiable from the available measurements?

provenance.scientific_neighbor: plant carbon allocation and potato tuber starch metabolism
provenance.source_boundary: The Starchforce name is project vocabulary. The stock-flow equations below are archive-generated formalization unless separately recovered from a primary Tim source.

authorship_boundary: No equation in this record should be attributed to Tim Dooley as an original equation unless a primary source is separately recovered. The model is a 2026-09-13 archive-generated scientific descendant.
state_space: K(t) >= 0, where K is one declared potato tuber starch/carbohydrate storage pool measured consistently through time.

variables.K: stored starch or declared carbohydrate pool per plant, tuber, dry-mass unit, or sampling unit
variables.J_in: net input into the declared storage pool
variables.J_out: mobilization/release flux from the pool into the declared target channel
variables.eta: first-order release coefficient in the linear model
variables.J_max: maximum release flux in the saturating candidate
variables.K_half: storage level at half-maximal saturating release

units.K: mass of starch/carbohydrate per declared sampling unit
units.J_in: same mass unit per unit time
units.J_out: same mass unit per unit time
units.rule: A fitted study must state the exact assay, normalization and time unit; symbolic quantities, bits and joules are not interchangeable with starch mass.

assumptions: The declared storage pool is sufficiently homogeneous for a one-compartment first model.
Flux definitions are non-overlapping so the same carbon is not counted twice.
The linear model assumes release and non-target loss are first-order in K over the fitted regime.
The saturating release law is a candidate extension, not a project axiom.
Environmental drivers may enter J_in or parameters only when measured and predeclared.
validity_regime: The one-pool model is intended as a low-dimensional approximation over a stated developmental window. It is not expected to represent every enzyme, compartment, cultivar, source-sink interaction or environmental response in potato physiology.

initial_and_boundary_conditions.initial: K(t0)=K0 from the first valid measurement or a fitted latent initial state with uncertainty.
initial_and_boundary_conditions.positivity: Model integration and fitting must preserve K>=0 and nonnegative physical fluxes unless a signed net-flux convention is explicitly declared.

exact_consequences_and_limits: For constant J0 in the linear model, the relaxation time is tau=1/(eta+Gamma).
If eta approaches zero, there is no target release channel and only Gamma removes material from the pool.
If Gamma approaches zero, depletion is controlled by the declared release channel.
If J_in approaches zero, the linear model predicts exponential depletion.
These statements are algebraic consequences of the chosen model, not independent biological discoveries.
observables: time-stamped tuber starch mass or concentration with normalization recorded
tuber dry mass and sampling unit
candidate source/input proxies such as assimilate supply where available
respiration or other loss measurements where available
developmental stage, cultivar, temperature, water status and treatment metadata
baselines: naive persistence: predict the next observed K from the previous K
constant-rate or simple exponential stock model
saturating release model only when held-out performance justifies its additional parameters

calibration.minimum_data: Repeated measurements across time with enough information to distinguish input from depletion; if J_in and losses are not independently constrained, eta and Gamma may be confounded.
calibration.fit: Use weighted least squares or a likelihood appropriate to the measurement error model.
calibration.uncertainty: Report confidence/credible intervals or bootstrap uncertainty for fitted parameters and predictions.
calibration.identifiability: Inspect parameter correlations/profile likelihood or equivalent diagnostics; do not report separately interpretable eta and Gamma if only their sum is identifiable.
calibration.validation: Reserve held-out times, plants or experimental conditions where sample size permits and compare predictive error rather than visual fit alone.
calibration.model_selection: Prefer the linear model unless the saturating model improves held-out prediction or a penalized criterion sufficiently to justify J_max and K_half.

falsifier: If the Starchforce-labelled model does not outperform an ordinary equally parameterized stock-flow baseline, violates mass balance, or requires non-identifiable parameters to obtain its apparent fit, then it has not earned status as a distinct scientific model in that application and should remain a project metaphor or naming layer.
promotion_rule: Remain T2 until actual potato data are fitted. Promotion to T3 requires a named dataset, reproducible preprocessing, fitted parameter constraints with uncertainty, baseline comparison and held-out or otherwise honest predictive evaluation.

scientific_sources.citation: Ahmad D, Ying Y, Bao J. Understanding starch biosynthesis in potatoes for metabolic engineering to improve starch quality: A detailed review. Carbohydrate Polymers 346 (2024) 122592.
scientific_sources.role: Current review establishing potato tuber starch as a major storage/energy reserve and summarizing starch biosynthesis.
